canonical_data: the working tree, per-task checkpoint repositories, and user-defined mode definitions
current_repo_note: Shut down in May 2026 and archived, with the extension delisted. Its own documentation names a community fork, Zoo Code, and its origin project as alternatives rather than declaring a successor, so the superseded status does not apply. That fork is excluded as packaging under the derivative rule, being identical to this record on every named field; a reader wanting a maintained agent in this lineage is served by the other published fork. It is the middle link between two published records, having forked from one and been forked into the other.
strengths: Per-task checkpoint repositories with navigation give genuine working-tree recovery, which its closest neighbours do not offer
A compatibility layer lets the same core run headless outside the editor, so one engine serves two front ends
Modes are first-class user-definable configuration with a published schema, giving reviewable role separation without a separate orchestration layer
weaknesses: Shut down in May 2026, with the repository archived and the extension delisted, so installing it now means building from source
Its command line auto-approves actions by default in interactive mode, inverting the safety posture the extension was known for
The live continuation is a community fork under different governance, so the reviewed privacy commitments no longer bind whoever ships the code
why_it_matters: The most widely installed editor coding agent to shut down mid-flight, and the middle link in a fork chain whose other two records the Atlas publishes.
